Thanks for the quick responses today. As we finalize procurement, our security and infra teams want a short architecture review focused on how Redwood's control plane will integrate with our VPC edge and on-prem data plane. Key items they called out:

- Control plane visibility (logs, audit streams) without opening inbound ports from internet

- KV cache persistence and whether any token material crosses our network boundary
- Failover behavior if the control plane loses reachability to the data plane

Can we schedule a 45-minute session this week to walk the architecture and a reference diagram? Also attaching our standard compliance checklist for context.

Thanks,

Putting the routing/sample NAT + SG snippets here before the call so Tara's team can review offline. Key notes:

- Data plane nodes (customer-managed) initiate all outbound connections to Redwood control plane endpoints over TLS (eg. *.control.redwood-inference.net), so no inbound rules needed on customer subnets.
- For low-latency private connectivity we support: VPC Peering (cross-account), Transit Gateway (for multi-VPC), and AWS PrivateLink (consumer will have an ENI in their VPC). PrivateLink removes route table exposure but requires NLB in our VPC.
- For peering/transit we recommend a dedicated route table for inference subnets and a strict NACL policy; avoid default SGs.

Sample route snippet (customer VPC):
- 10.0.10.0/24 -> local (data plane subnet)
- 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT GW (egress for package updates)
- 10.20.0.0/16 -> peer: redwood-inference-transit (for control plane reachable IPs via TGW)

Attachment: routing-table-samples.txt (txt)

Let me know any questions and I will have additional network ACL examples for the meeting.

Quick technical clarifications to seed the discussion:

- Control plane telemetry: we ship audit logs and metrics to the customer's log collector via a pull model (customer-configured forwarders) or via a push to an agreed endpoint. We never embed user prompts or model outputs in telemetry — keys and minimal metadata only.
- KV cache: ephemeral by default. For customers that require persisted caches inside their VPC we support mounting an S3-compatible store (customer-managed) over a private endpoint; nothing is stored in Redwood's multi-tenant store in that mode.
- Failover: if control plane becomes unreachable, the data plane continues to serve from local KV and model artifacts; we enforce a soft-sla for degraded mode and emit structured events for the customer's incident system. We recommend a healthcheck monitor to detect control-plane outages and an automated fallback to local-only mode.

I'll present a short slide on telemetry and KV options in the call.
— Karthik

Tara — thanks again for the call earlier today (notes below). Attaching the post-meeting checklist that maps your compliance items to our evidence and runbook.

Meeting notes / decisions:
- Selected PrivateLink for the initial pilot to avoid exposing route tables across accounts; Acme will provision the VPC endpoint and we will provide the NLB ARN and acceptance tests.
- Control plane telemetry will be delivered via a dedicated forwarder to Acme's Splunk collector; no model outputs or PII included in telemetry streams.
- KV cache: pilot will use ephemeral cache; persistent cache option deferred to phase 2 where Acme manages S3 behind a PrivateLink.
- Failover behavior documented: data plane will operate in local-only mode for up to 72 hours; Redwood will emit structured events to Acme's incident Slack channel and webhook.

Action items (owners):
- Acme: create PrivateLink endpoint and provide account ID by 2025-11-12
- Redwood (Dev): provide NLB ARN + acceptance test script by 2025-11-07
